title: Surge playbook + metrics slate
body:
Purpose:
A compact, action-first playbook for planned traffic surges (beta cohort opens /marketing bursts) with tied KPIs and explicit go/no-go triggers. This is a working slate — designed for 1:1 use by PM, Ops, SRE and CS during a ramp window.

High-level objective:
- Safely enable up to 100k MAU equivalent traffic spike across hosted + dedicated models for a 48h marketing blitz while keeping p50 latency <= 120ms and error rate < 0.5%.

Phase summary (rolling 7-day pre -> 72h live -> 7d post):
- Pre (T-7 -> T-1): verification, capacity staging, synthetic spike rehearsals.
- Live (T0 -> T+72h): phased traffic injection + live monitoring + rollback windows.
- Post (T+72h -> T+7): stability taper, cost reconciliation, postmortem.

Roadmap tracker snapshot (owner | milestone | ETA | status | blocking):
- Maya Chen | Surge kickoff sync + capacity allocation | 2026-02-25 | in_progress | waiting on infra quota approval (INFR-129)
- Priya Nair | Canary config (10% traffic, burst profile) | 2026-02-27 | ready | none
- Samir Patel | Autoscaler tune and max pool sizing | 2026-02-28 | in_review | SRE perf test results pending
- Diego Alvarez | Cost cap & billing alert rules | 2026-02-26 | done | n/a

KPI sheet (primary signals to watch) — rolling 5m windows, alert thresholds in parens:
- Ingress RPS (baseline 450 RPS, surge target 4500 RPS)
- p50 latency (<= 120ms)
- p95 latency (< 350ms)
- 5xx rate (< 0.5%)
- Tail queue depth (GPU queuing) (< 15 requests)
- Token cost per 1k (expected $1.8 during surge)
- Model fallback rate (< 2% of requests)
- Cache hit ratio (prefix KV) (> 45%)

Preflight checklist (clear ALL boxes before allowing >25% traffic):
- [ ] Capacity reservation confirmed on Dedicated pools (ticket INFR-129) — owner: Maya
- [ ] Canary route defined + telemetry hooks enabled — owner: Priya
- [ ] QoS and rate-limiter policies for new endpoints applied — owner: Platform Eng
- [ ] Fail-open policy verified for partial model unavailability — owner: Samir
- [ ] Cost burn guardrails & paging thresholds set — owner: Diego
- [ ] CS playbook updated with apology templates & credits — owner: Janelle
- [ ] Postmortem template attached to release runbook in Confluence — owner: Maya

Go / No-Go decision matrix (decision at T-0-2h):
- GREEN (go): p95 latency <= 300ms in last 30m; 5xx rate < 0.25%; autoscaler headroom >= 30%
- YELLOW (proceed with mitigations): p95 300–400ms OR 5xx 0.25–0.75% — reduce ramp rate to 50%, enable additional model fallback, notify execs
- RED (stop): p95 > 400ms OR 5xx > 0.75% OR observed cache hit < 20% — abort ramp, revert traffic to baseline, run incident runbook

Contingency actions (ranked):
1) Throttle non-essential routes (analytics, background scoring) — immediate
2) Switch traffic from hosted to dedicated mirror pool (if mirror healthy) — 5–10m
3) Reduce max sequence length and request tokens via on-the-fly policy — 2–5m
4) Engage model-variant fallback with coarser quantization (lower cost) — 1–3m
5) Full rollback to pre-surge routing (last resort) — 10–20m

Operational plays and owners during live window:
- Operations lead (Samir): run cadence checks, verify autoscaler logs every 15m
- SRE (Aleks Kovac): triage infra errors > 0.2% 5xx for 10m, escalate to infra on-call
- Product ops (Maya): coordinate CS comms, track KPI scoreboard, update execs every 30m
- CS (Janelle): respond to customers flagged by SLAs, prepare credits where needed
- Platform Eng (Priya): adjust queue limits, flip canary gates as needed

Simulation notes (recent runs):
- Synthetic spike run 2026-02-15: hit 3800 RPS sustained for 10m, p95 = 320ms, warm caches + autoscaler reacted with 22% latency improvement after second scale event.
- Edge-case: model-variant fallback introduced 2% additional errors due to tokenization mismatch — remedied by small tokenizer hotfix (PR #88).

Open questions / risks:
- Will marketing push exceed planned concurrency? Slack thread #marketing-burst has unconfirmed creative timing. (owner: Maya)
- Are there outstanding GPU driver updates scheduled during the surge window? (owner: Platform Eng)
- Cost overshoot tolerance from finance (query finance@redwood.ai for hard cap)

Postmortem & follow-ups (to run within 72h of cooldown):
- E2E timeline (who did what, timestamps) — owner: Maya
- Cost delta report vs forecast — owner: Diego
- Customer impact log + CS remediation ledger — owner: Janelle
- Action items tracked in JIRA label: POPS-SURGE-2026

Quick reference commands / links (for on-call):
- Metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/surge-playback
- Canary toggle: feature-flag:enable-surge-canary (ops-runbook link)
- Rollback play: docs.confluence/POPS/rollback-playbook

Next immediate steps (this doc is the canonical short-form for the run):
- Maya: confirm quota by 2026-02-24 EOD
- Priya: stage canary config and send traffic plan to SRE by 2026-02-25 09:00 PT
- Samir: run one full synthetic spike on 2026-02-26 02:00 PT and post logs to JIRA-POPS-482

Notes to self (work-in-progress tone):
- Keep checklist lightweight — ops should be able to run from phone.
- Save a trimmed copy for customer-facing postmortem (remove internal debug ids).

Document history:
- 2026-02-20: Created by Maya Chen (draft).
- 2026-02-24: Added canary plan and finance tags (Priya).
- 2026-03-10: Updated thresholds after latest sim (Samir).
